summary: Two source blockers: legacy live checkpoint handoff can lose its validated boundary; generator emits an incompatible legacy frozen-digest assertion. Core training frame loop and requested selection logic otherwise match the stated protocol at source level.

findings.title: The legacy latest.pt can be truncated or replaced between validation and SIGTERM
findings.details: The legacy trainer flushes its sequence log, then torch.save overwrites fit/latest.pt directly. Migration loads that live path at line 45 but does not preserve or resume that loaded object. After SIGTERM, it copies and reloads the live latest.pt at lines 57-65. A save can overlap the pre-stop read, start after that read, or be interrupted by the signal. The only recoverable latest file can then be incomplete. In addition, line 66 parses every post-stop log line before slicing to the saved count, so an incomplete uncommitted trailing line can abort migration after the trainer has already been stopped. This is a concrete conflicting read/write path, not a claim that corruption actually occurred.
findings.minimum_fix: In the migration helper only, capture one stable raw legacy checkpoint and raw sequence-log snapshot before SIGTERM; keep the raw bytes, fully CPU-deserialize and validate model/Adam/counts and the completed-sequence prefix before stopping. Verify snapshot stability against the same live file (identity/size/mtime and/or repeated byte SHA). If validation/stability fails, exit without signalling, without retry or fallback. After termination, resume only the pre-stop sealed snapshot; retain the post-stop legacy files as historical evidence even if incomplete. Do not edit the running legacy trainer or rewrite its old logs.

findings.title: The generator emits a trainer that rejects the explicitly supported legacy checkpoint
findings.details: The generator replaces the old before-state block with an unconditional frozen == resume['frozen_state_sha256'] assertion. The canonical legacy handoff deliberately sets frozen_state_sha256=None. Therefore a fresh generator-produced trainer fails before training. The actual generated trainer already contains the resume_RNG_saved/legacy-None branch. In-memory reconstruction of all six generated outputs found exactly this one difference: five outputs match byte-for-byte, trainer differs only by this branch.
findings.minimum_fix: Synchronize generator line 33 with the actual trainer's lines 79-82 legacy-None branch. Reconstruct the six outputs in memory and require exact equality. Preserve old M123 sources and historical protocol records.

A.name: Ground-truth provenance
A.details: Training targets originate from the pinned official Train152 groundtruth.txt paths, never from predictions. GT is loaded at sequence entry, but frame targets are consumed only after tracker.step has committed bbox/query/template action. C target is selected-frame real GT IoU, not future utility. OPE opens and hashes subsequent GT only after predictions and receipts exist; VOT uses toolkit dataset groundtruth through FrameMapSequence.

B.name: Score normalization
B.details: OPE precision averages overlaps over selected frames; recall divides overlap sum by dataset visibility count; curves macro-average by sequence; F uses the harmonic mean and returns raw plus percent values. Confidence-based thresholds and selecting the PR-curve maximum are explicit metric mechanics, not division by the model's own maximum. VOT EAO/ACC/ROB are multiplied by 100. Internal feature, depth-image and response calibration are not reported metric normalization.

C.name: File identity and result existence
C.details: All 26 intake file SHA values match. CurrentC captured F references exactly equal protocol [66.09145399091419,72.1632445464765] and use warm final cc71e0b4... . No M124 epoch result, migrated checkpoint, real OPE/VOT output or completed run is asserted. Future readers enforce result/receipt/plan/bundle/prediction SHA links. Actual raw remote artifacts and process state were not accessed.

D.name: Dead code and dispatch
D.details: The M124 controller dispatches training, both OPE trackers/analyzers, selection, selected-best VOT, sealing and collection. OPE evaluate_depthtrack_results and VOT failure collector have reachable call sites. Historical training/evaluation main functions imported for helpers remain main-guarded and are not called by the M124 route. The harmless depthtrack_pr.format_metrics helper is unused by this route. No function's existence is treated as evidence it ran.

E.name: Scope
E.details: Intended scope is one seed (2027), up to 20 completed Train152 epochs, complete 50/76373-frame and 80/101956-frame OPE after every completed epoch, and selected-best 127-sequence/1765-anchor VOT. External Test50/CDTB80 explicitly select checkpoints and stopping, so this is not untouched-test evaluation. Human initialization text review used multiframe aids. No training outcome, robustness, nine-metric success or runtime admission is established.

F.name: Evaluation type
F.details: Both OPE and VOT are intended real dataset-GT evaluations, with human-reviewed initialization text as an auxiliary input. They are not synthetic/model-reference proxies. M124 has no measured result in this audit.

protocol_checks.details: Pinned spec has 152 unique sequences and 219802 tracked frames per pass. All frames are tracked; valid GT only controls losses. No fit/dev selection or cached feature fit is dispatched. Own state is not reinitialized from subsequent GT.

protocol_checks.topic: Frozen pretrained models and two devices
protocol_checks.details: A/B and C are reconstructed on CUDA0, native STTrack and CLIP on CUDA1. Observation tensors move to the learning device; native/CLIP eval+requires_grad_(False)+no_grad and before/after digests guard frozen state. This is source reasoning, not a CUDA execution test.

Actual generated trainer loads model/Adam, checks sequence boundary, carries cumulative counters/records, restores saved Python/NumPy/CPU/all-CUDA RNG on new checkpoints. Legacy deliberately has no full frozen digest or RNG, and resets seed 2027 after reconstruction. The incomplete sequence is restarted. There is no bitwise-continuation claim. Migration safety remains blocked by B1.

protocol_checks.topic: Epoch completion and complete OPE counts
protocol_checks.details: Epoch completion requires epoch*152 records and epoch*219802 tracking calls before final publication. Both OPE datasets run and counts/SHA are checked before selection or next training epoch.

protocol_checks.topic: Warm comparison, strict dual-decline stop, equal-mean best and ties
protocol_checks.details: Initial previous F values are the supplied warm reference; first trained epoch is eligible even if below warm. Two adjacent transitions with both scores strictly lower trigger stop. Any equality or one-score rise resets streak. Best uses equal mean; strict > preserves earliest tie. Five pure-Python fixtures passed.

protocol_checks.topic: One selected epoch weight shared across OPE and VOT
protocol_checks.details: Best final.pt is copied and SHA checked; VOT plan reuses that epoch's fit/evaluation bundle; OPE/VOT result identities all compare to the same final and bundle SHA. Four VOT shards require all 1765 trajectories and 5295 files.

protocol_checks.topic: Old process target and hourly boundary
protocol_checks.details: Migration checks its request deadline before live access; the captured original deadline is 2026-10-11T15:34:49.891541+00:00. It reads /proc/<requested PID>/cmdline and checks old trainer script/output before SIGTERM; old stage must record -15 and controller nonzero, and process path must disappear. Actual MIGRATION_REQUEST and PID birth/current parent identity are not supplied or attested, so this is not permission to stop a process.

protocol_checks.topic: Source seal, dispatch paths and role imports
protocol_checks.details: Source/input maps and review report are hashed before launch, inference checks bundle source identities, and generated VOT wrapper/config/metadata are sealed. Metric-role top-level imports remain stdlib/NumPy plus lazy runtime definitions; Torch/CLIP/CUDA construction is inside tracking paths. Exact future deployed copies/import resolution and installed package versions are not inspected. The future request must pin the actual dispatched new code-root dependencies, not merely old source paths.

Entire old/new per-frame action, AB loss, C IoU/MSE loss, accumulation, clipping and Adam update loop are structurally identical by AST. Models and tracker helpers are reused. Only lifecycle/resume/checkpoint/evaluation orchestration changes. C inputs are detached, so this is joint optimization of A+B and C, not temporal end-to-end backpropagation.

Five of six deterministic generated outputs exactly match actual bytes. The trainer mismatch is precisely B2. Four additional M124 controller/migration/selection/supervisor sources are separately authored, not generated by this script.

No source mutation is performed by migration; handoff creates separate copies. This audit itself modifies only its designated output directory and snapshots all 63 inspected inputs. Current R1 cannot certify a future actual stop/copy/launch.

evidence_limits: Source-only audit: no SSH/network access, GPU query, training/NN forward, checkpoint deserialization, dataset traversal, remote process query/signal, or source/intake mutation was performed.

No M124 migration request, deployed new code-root, live PID state, real checkpoint bytes or actual M124 epoch/OPE/VOT artifacts were supplied or executed. Source checks are not runtime admission and not proof of performance.

Legacy M123 checkpoints omit RNG and full frozen-model digest. Seed reset plus repeating the partial sequence is explicit; neither this migration nor later RNG storage retrospectively makes it bitwise continuous.

Exactly 26 intake files were fully read; local import closure and relevant dynamically dispatched metric/native/bridge dependencies were followed. Whole installed Torch/CLIP/VOT/CUDA packages and every transitive native backbone helper were not attested. Historical helper main bodies outside the dispatched path were parsed/hashed, not exhaustively re-audited.

Five initially discovered local overlay/config candidates have hashes different from the pinned remote runtime or no applicable pin. They remain recorded and snapshotted as non-authoritative candidates; matching official/native source snapshots were separately found and read. They are not substituted for pinned runtime code.

The pinned OPE implementation is a local VOT-style PR implementation. This review reads its normalization/GT code, but does not establish upstream official-toolkit byte equivalence or recompute current scores from raw 130-sequence predictions/GT.
CurrentC captured warm metrics only establish literal agreement with the requested initial reference. Historical CurrentC results are not M124 results and were not freshly numerically recomputed.
Test50/CDTB80 are explicitly used to select epoch and stopping. No untouched-test, multiple-seed robustness or nine-metric target-achievement claim is supported.
Human-reviewed initialization text uses multiframe aids. It must not be relabeled as blind first-frame-only human review.
The exact actual reviewer model/reasoning/backend is UNATTESTED by native receipts available to this child. Requested route is gpt-6-astra/max; review remains same-family and provisional.

Native exec_command exposes combined stdout/stderr. Traces preserve it verbatim and explicitly mark separate stderr unavailable. Initial mandatory session-context read exceeded output budget and is preserved as returned, including truncation. Subsequent source reads and deterministic source checks were bounded; transcript contains two audit tooling errors corrected by explicit installed Python and UTF-8, without target code execution.
Trace files contain the mandatory initial local user/session context read and must remain private/project-local, not published. Reports contain only task-relevant evidence.

Future source seal validation must use the actual dispatched paths and review report identity. Looping over a source map does not independently attest import resolution or an absent deployment package.
Per-epoch parameter-change reporting compares final state with warm initialization, not the immediate prior epoch; it supports cumulative change only.
